#1897

The JSON-RPC envelope converter matches `jsonrpc`/`id`/`method`/`params`/`result`/`error` exactly, but the typed contents of `params` and `result` were deserialized with the internal source-generated `JsonContext`, which is declared with `JsonSerializerDefaults.Web` and therefore binds property names case-insensitively. A `tools/call` request with `params.Name` was dispatched as if it were `params.name`, even though middleware or proxies inspecting `params.name` would not recognize it. Some transports and the Tasks extension also deserialized protocol types through the case-insensitive `DefaultOptions`, so fields such as `error.Code` or a task-based `CallToolResult.IsError` were bound regardless of casing.

## Changes

- `McpJsonUtilities.JsonContext` now sets `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = false`. Protocol DTOs (requests, results and notifications, on both client and server) only bind the property names defined by the specification, consistent with the envelope.
- New public `McpJsonUtilities.ProtocolOptions`: a cached, read-only copy of `DefaultOptions` with case-sensitive property matching. It is built from the same source-generated context, so trimming and Native AOT behave as before. Consumers deserializing protocol messages themselves can use it.
- The protocol readers that went through options now use `ProtocolOptions`: the stdio client and server transports (`StreamClientSessionTransport`, `StreamServerTransport`), the ASP.NET Core Streamable HTTP and SSE request reader (`StreamableHttpHandler`), and every protocol type in `ModelContextProtocol.Extensions.Tasks` (task-based `CallToolResult`, `InputRequest`, `IDictionary<string, InputResponse>`, `JsonRpcErrorDetail`). The HTTP client transports already used the case-sensitive context.
- `McpJsonUtilities.DefaultOptions` explicitly keeps `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true`. It is also used for user-defined types (tool, prompt and resource parameters, `McpClientTool` arguments, `SendRequestAsync<TParameters, TResult>`), so binding of user data is unchanged. Its XML docs now point to `ProtocolOptions` and state that protocol types deserialized through `DefaultOptions` keep case-insensitive matching.

As discussed in the issue, this is exact protocol-field matching, not new validation of non-canonical JSON:

| `tools/call` params | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `{"Name":"echo"}` | dispatched to `echo` | `name` missing, JSON-RPC error, handler not invoked |
| `{"name":"echo","Name":"other"}` | last value wins (`other`) | `echo` |
| `{"Name":"other","name":"echo"}` | `echo` | `echo` |
| `{"name":"echo","Arguments":{...}}` | arguments bound | arguments not bound (`null`) |
| `{"name":"echo","arguments":{"text":"a","Text":"B"}}` | both keys kept | both keys kept (user data) |

Fields with defaults keep their defaults when only an alternately cased key is present; for example a `CallToolResult` with only `Content` still ends up with an empty `content` list rather than failing.

## Compatibility and release notes

- `McpApps.SerializerOptions` now derives from `ProtocolOptions`, retaining the Apps source-generated context. Apps extension fields such as `resourceUri` and `mimeTypes` are case-sensitive, consistent with `GetUiCapability`. Alternate-cased fields are ignored, and canonical fields win in either property order. Correctly cased JSON, serialization output, strongly typed C# usage, `DefaultOptions`, and caller-supplied options remain unchanged. The Apps guide and XML documentation describe this intentional compatibility change.
- The OAuth metadata types live in the same source-generated context, so their parsing also becomes case-sensitive. Worth mentioning in the release notes together with the protocol change.

## Tests

- Nested content reads now resolve annotation and icon metadata from the supplied serializer options, preserving opt-in case-insensitive matching. Actual client API tests also cover canonical tool-result fields through ordinary, immediate-task and polled-task paths.

- `McpServerTests.Call_Tool_Request_Params_Are_Matched_Case_Sensitively` sends raw `tools/call` requests through the server: `Name` only (rejected, handler not invoked), alternately cased `Arguments` (not bound), canonical, both key orders with `name` and `Name`, and alternately cased keys inside `arguments` (preserved as distinct entries).
- `McpJsonUtilitiesTests`: `ProtocolOptions` is a read-only singleton with case-sensitive matching; for a JSON-RPC error with both `code`/`message` and `Code`/`Message`, and for a `CallToolResult` with `Content`/`IsError`, `ProtocolOptions` binds only the canonical names while `DefaultOptions` keeps the previous behavior. `DefaultOptions_MatchesPropertyNamesCaseInsensitively` still covers user types.
- `StdioServerTransportTests.ReadMessagesAsync_Should_Match_Error_Properties_Case_Sensitively` reads such an error line through the stdio transport.
- `McpServerToolTests.BindsNestedArgumentPropertiesCaseInsensitively` invokes a tool whose parameter is a nested user DTO, bound from `LOCATION`/`CITY`, to confirm user-data binding is unchanged.

The server and stdio transport tests failed without the earlier core change. The earlier core revision was tested on net10.0 (Windows): `ModelContextProtocol.Tests` 2414 passed / 6 skipped and `ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore.Tests` 636 passed / 31 skipped. Those counts are historical, not a full-suite run of the latest head.

For the earlier Apps follow-up (historical), `dotnet test tests/ModelContextProtocol.Tests/ModelContextProtocol.Tests.csproj -f net10.0 --filter FullyQualifiedName~McpAppsTests -p:JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false` passed all 39 tests on Windows using SDK 10.0.401 / runtime 10.0.12. The nine new cases cover canonical and alternate spellings, both property orders, agreement with `GetUiCapability`, and caller-controlled options. The net9.0 target compiled, but its test host could not start because the local .NET 9 runtime is absent. Other target frameworks, platforms and the full suite were not rerun locally for this follow-up. The latest upstream Build and Test, CodeQL and Markdown-link workflows await maintainer approval.

As noted in the issue, this is a subtle behavior change for peers that relied on alternate casing, so it probably belongs in a minor release.

cc @tarekgh for review

## Latest review follow-up (2026-10-22)

Commit `0d92883b1a3778e6fe922e73556c0724ecbdffb0` resolves nested annotation and icon contracts from the converter's supplied options. Twelve regression cases cover canonical/alternate nested fields through DefaultOptions, ProtocolOptions, and explicit case-insensitive caller options. Six client API cases cover ordinary tool results, immediate Tasks results, and a working-then-completed Tasks poll, with canonical content/isError winning over alternate spellings in either property order.

Validation on Windows with SDK 10.0.101:

- The 18-case regression selection on the previous head reproduces four nested-options failures; the six client reader cases already pass. After the fix, the broader net9.0 selection passes 191 cases with reflection disabled by the repository's target configuration.
- Complete ModelContextProtocol.Tests, Execution!=Manual: net10.0 passes 2,453 cases with 4 skips. The net9.0 initial run passes 2,452, fails one external Node test-server launch, and skips 4. After installing the pinned npm dependencies, the failed test's two-case method passes on net9.0. This is a targeted rerun, not a second complete net9.0 suite.
- The previous Windows CI failure families were selected locally on net10.0: 5 pass, 1 expected skip, after setting NO_PROXY for loopback to keep the in-memory transport off the local proxy. This does not establish the cause of the earlier upstream failures or replace the complete ASP.NET Core suite.
- net8.0, .NET Framework, other operating systems, and the complete ASP.NET Core suite were not run for this follow-up. Earlier test counts and model/runtime details above are historical. New-head upstream workflows currently require maintainer approval; local results do not imply CI success.

> [!NOTE]
> This follow-up summary and the code/tests were prepared with AI assistance. The reported checks were executed locally.

## Standalone-context compatibility follow-up (2026-10-23)

Commit `f7017ba6d4d6a4e480ba746bea7b7c0cf461b8f5` restores nested content reads for standalone source-generated contexts that register only `ContentBlock` or `CallToolResult`. Caller resolvers take precedence over an SDK-generated fallback, including nested audience and icon-size metadata. Caller settings/converters are copied, the caller's options are not modified, and only read-only options are cached; direct calls with mutable options observe later changes.

Eighteen regression cases cover standalone contexts, canonical/alternate nested casing, caller contracts, and mutable options. The initial 17-case selection on the previous head produced 16 missing-metadata failures and one passing caller-contract control. Final-source Windows/SDK 10.0.101 validation passes 160 focused cases on each of net9.0 and net10.0, with System.Text.Json reflection disabled for net9.0.

The complete final-source project suite, full ASP.NET Core suite, other frameworks/platforms, and Native AOT publish/link were not completed for this follow-up. Earlier full-suite counts above are historical. Local results do not establish upstream CI success. This follow-up and its tests were prepared with AI assistance; the reported checks were executed locally.
